Data & Privacy

How we handle your data

Your data is yours, and we build so it stays that way — much of the work never touches your real data at all.

Sample-first by default

Most of an automation is structure — how something is read, sorted, and drafted. That part can be built and tested against samples or made-up examples, often with no real data of yours involved at all.

Real data — only to test, only before handover

When it's time to prove the automation works end to end, we may need to use your real data. That happens in a defined, limited window before handover: used only to test, then cleared. It is never kept beyond that work, and never shared.

Live — in your systems

Once it's running, the automation works in or alongside your own systems. We only ever touch what a given task needs.

What we never do

  • Keep your data beyond the work
  • Share it with anyone
  • Use it for anything other than the job you asked for

What an AI service sees

You decide what, if anything, an outside AI service is ever shown. Sensitive work — finance, legal, health — is handled with stricter limits on what leaves your environment.

A person approves every step

Nothing is sent, paid, or filed on its own. That human step isn't only reassurance — it's also what the rules below expect of automated decisions that affect people.

The rules we work to

revDSG — Switzerland's data-protection law, in force since September 2023. It sets how personal data must be handled: used only for a clear purpose, kept secure, not kept longer than needed, and open to the person it concerns.

GDPR — the EU's equivalent. It applies when a business serves or monitors people in the EU. Because we work with clients worldwide, we build to both.

Both expect a human in the loop for automated decisions that significantly affect someone — a review a person can ask for. Our approve-every-step design is that review, built in.

Working together

When we handle data on your behalf, we sign a data-processing agreement — you as the controller, us as the processor — that puts all of this in writing. Ask us for it any time.

This page describes how we work; it isn't legal advice. For your own obligations, your lawyer or fiduciary is the right guide.
